tagline: Up the braided Matanuska from the colony farms to four ranges.
intro: Out of Anchorage the Glenn runs northeast with the Chugach Mountains alongside, the whole way. Past Palmer it enters the glacier-cut canyon of the Matanuska River and follows the braided river for more than half its 135 miles, by the old coal camp of Sutton and up to Eureka Summit, at 3,332 feet the high point of the highway.
The road was made for farmers. It began in the 1930s as the Palmer Road, built to reach a new agricultural colony, and the war carried it on to Glennallen. It was paved in the 1950s.

moments.title: Palmer
moments.text: In May 1935, 203 families from the Iron Range of Michigan, Minnesota and Wisconsin arrived here, spent their first summer in a tent city and drew lots for 40-acre farms.

moments.title: Matanuska Glacier
moments.text: Twenty-seven miles of ice come down near the road and feed the river, moving about a foot a day. The park is public. The only bridge into it charges a toll.

moments.title: Eureka Summit
moments.text: On the divide between the Chugach and the Talkeetnas the byway ends with the Alaska Range and the Wrangell-St. Elias Mountains also in sight.
